How Autonomous AI Agents & Vector Embeddings Work (under the hood) ⚡
Docker vs VM: same server, how many apps fit?

• VMs: a whole OS each → heavier CPU/RAM overhead
• Containers: share the host kernel → lighter isolation
• Kernel sharing changes density: more apps per box
• Rule of thumb: VM = stronger OS boundary; container = faster packing

Practical takeaway: If you’re interviewing, describe the isolation trade-off (kernel vs full OS) and tie it to reliability/SRE goals.

Debate question: When building LLM systems + tools, should you default to VMs for “safety” or containers for “scale” — and why?

Docker vs VM isn’t just deployment trivia—it’s an architecture decision that affects how you run LLM system components (vector DB/search services, agent tool runners, queues, and inference gateways).

VMs (Virtual Machines)
• Each VM includes a full guest OS.
• Pros: stronger separation at the OS boundary; familiar operational model.
• Cons: higher overhead → fewer workloads per host; slower boot; more “moving OS” surface.

Containers (Docker/LXC)
• Containers share the host kernel; each container has its own userspace.
• Pros: higher density (e.g., “host full” with VMs vs many containers sharing the kernel), faster start, and more consistent packaging for microservices.
• Cons: isolation is different—if the host kernel is compromised, multiple containers can be impacted.

Production pattern for autonomous AI agents + vector embeddings
• Separate concerns: agent runtime, embedding/indexing pipelines, and similarity search (vector store) as distinct services.
• Use containers to maximize packing/iteration speed; use VMs when you need stronger OS-level isolation (e.g., multi-tenant risk, compliance boundaries, or heterogeneous kernel requirements).
• Add guardrails: resource limits (cgroups), network policies, and staged rollouts for inference + embedding jobs.

If you’re building for reliability: decide isolation level based on threat model and operational cost, then standardize your orchestration (Kubernetes/managed equivalents) and observability.
